summary: The first focusable thing on the page: a keyboard user's way past the header and navigation, straight to the content. Hidden until it has focus.
useWhen: every page of an app with a header or navigation before its content — one, first in the body, pointing at <main>

useInstead.when: a link to a section further down the same page
useInstead.why: a table of contents or an in-page link is always visible; a skip link exists only for the keyboard, only at the top

composition.note: Render it once, in the app shell, as the very first element in the body: before banners, before the Header. `target` is the `id` of the page's <main>. It moves focus to the target itself rather than following `#id`, so it works under a hash router; a target that is not focusable gets `tabindex="-1"` while it holds focus, and the next Tab continues from inside it. Its words default to "Skip to main content"; pass children only to translate them. It is fixed at the window's top-left above everything while focused, so where it sits in the shell's layout does not matter.

children.note: optional; the default is "Skip to main content"

guarantees: the first Tab on a freshly loaded page reaches it, and it is shown, above anything fixed on the page, while it has focus
activating it puts focus inside the content: the next Tab is the content's first control, not the Header's
it leaves the URL alone, so a hash route is not replaced by `#main`
hidden by clipping, not `display: none`, so it stays in the tab order
requires: an element with the `target` id — the page's <main> — rendered on every page the link is
notes: It satisfies WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks. A missing target falls back to following the link, so it is never a dead control. After an in-app navigation the app's own focus management decides where focus goes; the skip link is for a fresh load and for anyone who returns to the top.

antiPatterns.dont: a skip link after the Header or the banners
antiPatterns.why: it is only useful as the first stop: a keyboard user has already tabbed through what it was meant to skip

antiPatterns.dont: `<a href="#main">` by hand in an app with a hash router
antiPatterns.why: following `#main` replaces the route: the page changes, or the router shows its not-found screen

antiPatterns.dont: several skip links, to each section
antiPatterns.why: a list of stops before the content is a second navigation to tab through; headings and landmarks already let a screen reader jump between sections
